title: Advanced Scenic Design
description: This course builds upon tools learned in THTR 22: Beginning Set Design to increase fluency in scenic design approaches and techniques. Focusing on building ideas from texts and music, you will evolve design approaches through research and critiques. Designs will culminate in scale models and supporting materials. Projects in THTR 122 will focus on opera, dance, and musical theatre with unique scenic demands including multiple locations, period detail, and awareness of performance styles and conventions.

title: Advanced Stage Lighting Design
description: Lecture-demonstration of controllable properties and functions of light. Includes technical drawing: light plots, scheduling and organization for lighting design, drawing using light and shadow, perspective drawing. Practical application through studio exercise.

title: Design Portfolio
description: This course will introduce students to advanced topics in the art and craft of visual media design for projection and video with an emphasis on live performance.

title: Advanced Costume Design
description: In this course students will receive an advance and detailed perspective on the art of costume design. Through four different projects, they will explore different character development experiences, with a continued focus on thematic storytelling. Together, students will learn how to craft character, while focusing on the scope of a full production.

title: Advanced Makeup
description: Emphasis on methods of character makeup, special effects, and new prosthetics construction and application techniques.

title: Theatre Rendering Techniques
description: Advanced theatre rendering techniques for the theatre designer. Continued development in drawing and use of different mediums. Concentration on rendering light, shadow, and texture.

title: Painting for the Stage
description: Advanced work in scenic painting including special textures, foliage, trompe-l'oeil effects as used for stage.

title: History of Design and Production
description: A survey of the evolution of design styles and production trends in western theatre, emphasizing the history of design and designers.

title: Advanced Costume Construction
description: Exploration of advanced draping, drafting, and tailoring technqiues used in theatrical costume design.

title: Advanced Costume Techniques
description: Exploration of advanced costume crafts techniques including pattern development as it related to corset construction. Period undergarment research and construction. Subject matter varies by quarter.

title: History of Decorative Styles
description: A survey of the evolution of design styles and production trends in western theater, emphasizing the history of design and designers, including a study of both interior and exterior decoration with concentration on furnishing, accessories and the changing patterns of culture.

title: History of Costume I
description: A survey of the development of western clothing and costume from Biblical times to the Restoration as related to the changing patterns of culture. Short survey of non-Western clothing and costume.

title: History of Costume II
description: A survey of the development of western clothing and costume from early Georgian to the present as related to the changing patterns of culture. Short survey of non-Western clothing and costume.

title: Advanced Theatrical Crafts
description: Concentration on special materials and technique utilized in theatrical productions including decorative and three-dimensional art.

title: Puppet Design and Construction
description: Explores the history of various puppet styles and will focus on the design and creation of three iconic puppet forms: Thai shadow puppets (Nang yai), rod puppets (Bunraku), and marionettes. Students will learn both the mechanical aspects and the artistic design elements of puppet creation by creating one of each of these three styles.

title: Advanced Acting Workshop I
description: Advanced exploration, performances, and criticism of scenes from a broad range of dramatic scripts with focus on the actor's perspective.

title: Advanced Acting Workshop II
description: Further exploration of performances and criticism of scenes from a broad range of dramatic scripts with focus on the actor's perspective.

title: Shakespeare Basics
description: Theater 141, Shakespeare Basics, provides the tools for analyzing and acting Shakespearean text. This is an actors approach. Through the study of sense, scansion/rhythm, phrasing, speech units, word structure, figures of speech, key words, imagery, reception/impact, physical action, inner and outer focal points the student lays the groundwork for interpreting and embodying Shakespeare characters. While this course serves as a basic entry to Shakespeare, the student is expected to have some experience or training as an actor and familiar with the terms objective, given circumstances, intention, personalization, and subtext.

title: I.V. Live
description: This course produces a weekly performance series in Isla Vista. Students get first-hand experience in the rigors of theatrical production, as they learn to execute all logistical, technical and promotional details. The course is affiliated with Isla Vista Arts.

title: The People's Voice
description: Students and teens from the community collaborate in writing, crafting, and performing an epic myth through the lens of their personal stories.

title: Shakespeare Production
description: Students study, rehearse and produce one of Shakespeare's plays. The class culminates with performances that are open to the public during the final week. Students can participate as actors, assistant directors, designers or stage managers.

title: Shakespeare Production
description: Students study, rehearse and produce one of Shakespeare's plays. The class culminates with performances that are open to the public during the final week. Students can participate as actors, assistant directors, designers or stage managers.

title: Oregon Shakespeare Festival Tour
description: Students study one or more plays being performed at the Oregon Shakespeare Festival. While in Ashland, students attend 7-8 performances, take a backstage tour and participate in workshops and lectures led by members of the company.

title: Launch Pad: New Plays in Process
description: Working with the artistic director of LAUNCH PAD and 3 professional playwrights, this 3-week intensive course workshops a new play every week. Student actors, directors, designers, dramaturgs, playwrights, and stage managers learn the vital skills of working on new plays in the earliest stages of their development. The workshop culminates in an invited public reading at the end of each week. Over the 3 weeks, participants have the opportunity to take on different functions in the process.

title: Theatre Workshop
description: Projects in costume, scenery, lighting, acting, directing.

title: Advanced Acting
description: Scene work and exercises exploring various acting styles which may include Shakespeare, Boal, Artaud, Greek, period comedy and farce, and Absurd.
prerequisites_raw: Theater 15C and 188S; concurrent enrollment in Theater 110A and 111A. Consent of instructor.

title: Advanced Acting
description: Scene work and exercises exploring various acting styles which may include Shakespeare, Boal, Artaud, Greek, period comedy and farce, and Absurd.
prerequisites_raw: Theater 15C and 188S; concurrent enrollment in Theater 110B and 111B. Consent of instructor.

title: Advanced Acting
description: Scene work and exercises exploring various acting styles which may include Shakespeare, Boal, Artaud, Greek, period comedy and farce, and Absurd
prerequisites_raw: Theater 15C and 188S; concurrent enrollment in Theater 110C and 111C. Consent of instructor.

title: Advanced Acting: Modern Trends
description: Study and performance of contemporary acting developments.

title: Senior Auditions
description: Preparation and study of material and techniques for professional and graduate school audition.

title: Alternate Acting Styles
description: Continued work in performance styles and other skills.
